uncited: It serves as the foundational 2D case for the [Marching Cubes](774-marching-cubes.md) algorithm.
*   **Input:** A 2D scalar field grid `Grid` of size $N_x \times N_y$ (rows $\times$ columns), where each cell contains a scalar value.
*   **Edge/Segment:** A pair of 2D points $(p_1, p_2)$.
**Evaluate Corners:** Retrieve the scalar values at the four corners of the current cell.
*   If $C = 0$ (all corners below isovalue) or $C = 15$ (all corners above isovalue), no intersection occurs.
**Determine Intersections:** For non-trivial cases ($1 \le C \le 14$), determine which edges of the square are intersected by the isosurface.
**Interpolate Intersection Points:** For each intersected edge, calculate the exact intersection point using linear interpolation.
*   **Single Corner Cases (1, 2, 4, 8):** One corner is inside.
*   **Opposite Corner Cases (3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12):** Two opposite corners are inside.
*   **Adjacent Corner Cases (7, 11, 13, 14):** Three corners are inside (equivalent to one outside).
*   **Boundary Conditions:** The algorithm iterates up to $N_x - 2$ and $N_y - 2$, assuming the grid includes the outer boundary vertices.
*   **Degenerate Input:** If a corner value exactly equals the `IsoValue`, the sign check `(v >= isovalue)` treats it as "inside".
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N_x N_y)$ for the input grid.
Output size is proportional to the number of intersected cells.
*   **When to use:** Extracting 2D contours from scalar fields (e.g., height maps, 2D simulations, slice extraction from 3D volumes).

*   **When not to use:** For 3D volumes (use [Marching Cubes](774-marching-cubes.md)) or when high-fidelity smooth surfaces are required without post-processing (consider [Marching Tetrahedra](1733-marching-tetrahedra.md) for better normal estimation).
Marching Squares is the 2D analog of the Marching Cubes algorithm.
It was developed as a standard technique for contouring 2D scalar fields.
The algorithm processes each square cell independently, determining the intersection of the isosurface with the cell edges based on the vertex values.
It is widely used in image processing, geographic information systems (GIS) for contour lines, and as a component in 3D volume rendering pipelines for extracting 2D slices.
